r: Little golden madeleines with their characteristic bump, flavoured with butter and lemon.
Whisk the eggs and sugar until the mixture turns pale.
Add the lemon zest, flour, baking powder and a pinch of salt, then the melted butter.
Chill the batter for 1 h. This is the secret of the bump.|Rest|60
Preheat the oven to 220 °C. Fill the buttered moulds three-quarters full.
Bake for 5 min, turn the oven down to 180 °C and bake for another 5 min.|Oven|10
With cocoa in the batter and a chocolate base.
Cocoa madeleines, with a chocolate shell at the bottom of the mould.
Whisk the eggs and sugar, then add the flour, cocoa, baking powder and melted butter.
Preheat the oven to 220 °C. Fill the buttered moulds and bake for 5 min, then 5 min at 180 °C.|Oven|10
Melt the chocolate, pour a little into each clean mould and set the madeleines on top.
Leave to set in the fridge for 20 min before turning out.|Rest|20
Some of the sugar is replaced with honey.
Softer madeleines with a lovely honey flavour.
Whisk the eggs and sugar, then add the honey.
Add the flour and baking powder, then the lukewarm melted butter.
Preheat the oven to 220 °C, fill the buttered moulds and bake for 5 min, then 5 min at 180 °C.|Oven|10
The Breton cake made with four ingredients in equal weights: eggs, sugar, flour and butter.
Preheat the oven to 180 °C and butter a loaf tin.
Whisk the eggs and sugar until pale.
Add the flour, baking powder and a pinch of salt, then the melted butter.
Pour into the tin and bake for 40 min. A knife blade should come out dry.|Oven|40
With diced apples in the batter.
A soft pound cake with pieces of tender apple.
Preheat the oven to 180 °C. Peel and dice the apples.
Whisk the eggs and sugar, add the flour, baking powder and cinnamon, then the melted butter.
Fold in the apples and pour into a buttered tin.
Flavoured with orange zest and juice.
A very gentle pound cake with an orange scent.
Whisk the eggs and sugar, then add the orange zest and juice.
Add the flour and baking powder, then the melted butter.
Pour into a buttered loaf tin and bake for 40 min.|Oven|40
The vanilla and chocolate loaf cake with pretty swirls, just like the one from tea time.
Preheat the oven to 180 °C and butter a loaf tin.
Whisk the melted butter, sugar and vanilla sugar, then add the eggs one by one.
Add the flour, baking powder and milk.
Split the batter in two and add the cocoa to one half.
Pour the batters into the tin in alternating layers and run a fork through to marble.
Less butter: a yoghurt keeps it soft.
A lighter marble cake that is just as soft.
Mix the yoghurt, sugar and eggs, then the flour, baking powder and oil.
Split the batter in two and add the cocoa to one half.
Pour in alternating layers into an oiled tin and marble with a fork.
The pale part is flavoured with orange.
The chocolate and orange duo in a very simple marble cake.
Whisk the melted butter and sugar, add the eggs, then the flour and baking powder.
Split the batter: orange zest and juice in one half, cocoa in the other.
Pour in alternating layers into a buttered tin and marble with a fork.
The American loaf cake made with very ripe bananas, soft and fragrant.
Mash the bananas with a fork.
Mix them with the eggs, sugar and melted butter.
Add the flour, baking powder and cinnamon without mixing too much.
Pour into a buttered loaf tin and bake for 50 min.|Oven|50
The indulgent banana bread, full of melting chocolate chips.
Mash the bananas and mix them with the eggs, sugar and melted butter.
Add the flour and baking powder, then the chocolate chips.
Pour into a loaf tin and bake for 50 min.|Oven|50
Very ripe bananas are enough to sweeten it.
A soft, light cake sweetened only by the fruit.
Mash the bananas and mix them with the eggs and melted oil.
Add the flour, oats, baking powder and cinnamon.
Pour into a loaf tin and bake for 45 min.|Oven|45
The creamy cheesecake on a biscuit base, baked gently in the oven.
Preheat the oven to 160 °C. Crush the biscuits and mix them with the melted butter.
Press this mixture into the bottom of a springform tin.
Whisk the cream cheese, sugar, cream and lemon zest, then the eggs one by one.
Pour over the base and bake for 1 h.|Oven|60
Leave to cool in the oven with the door ajar, then chill for at least 4 h.
Set in the fridge, with no oven.
A fresh, light cheesecake you make the day before.
Crush the biscuits, mix with the melted butter and press into the bottom of a springform tin.
Whip the very cold cream until thick.
Mix the cream cheese, icing sugar and lemon juice, then fold in the whipped cream.
Spread over the base and leave to set in the fridge for at least 6 h.
With a berry sauce on top.
The creamy cheesecake, covered with a berry sauce.
Preheat the oven to 160 °C. Press the crushed biscuits and butter into the bottom of a tin.
Whisk the cream cheese, 150 g of sugar and the cream, then the eggs.
Pour over the base and bake for 1 h. Leave to cool, then chill for 4 h.|Oven|60
Cook the berries for 10 min with the rest of the sugar, then leave to cool.|Cooking|10
Cover the cheesecake with the sauce just before serving.

a: carrot cake with cream cheese frosting
r: The soft cake with carrots and spices, with its cream cheese frosting.
Preheat the oven to 180 °C. Finely grate the carrots.
Whisk the eggs, brown sugar and oil.
Add the flour, baking powder and cinnamon, then the carrots.
Pour into a buttered tin and bake for 45 min. Leave to cool.|Oven|45
Whisk the cream cheese and icing sugar, and spread this frosting over the cake.
With chopped walnuts in the batter and on the frosting.
The carrot cake, even more indulgent, with crunchy walnuts.
Preheat the oven to 180 °C. Grate the carrots and roughly chop the walnuts.
Whisk the eggs, sugar and oil, then add the flour, baking powder and cinnamon.
Add the carrots and two-thirds of the walnuts.
Pour into a tin and bake for 45 min. Leave to cool.|Oven|45
Cover with the cream cheese and icing sugar frosting, then the rest of the walnuts.
No frosting, with less sugar and oil.
A soft carrot cake for an everyday snack.
Preheat the oven to 180 °C. Grate the carrots.
Whisk the eggs, sugar, oil and yoghurt.
Add the flour, baking powder and cinnamon, then the carrots.
Pour into a loaf tin and bake for 45 min.|Oven|45
Little almond and brown butter cakes, crisp outside and soft inside.
Heat the butter until it is golden and smells of hazelnuts.|Cooking|5
Mix the ground almonds, icing sugar and flour, then the unwhisked egg whites.
Add the lukewarm brown butter and fill the buttered moulds.
With a raspberry in the middle of each financier.
The almond financiers, with a tart raspberry.
Preheat the oven to 200 °C and brown the butter.|Cooking|5
Mix the ground almonds, icing sugar, flour and egg whites.
Add the brown butter and fill the moulds.
Press one or two raspberries into each financier.
With cocoa in the batter and chocolate chips.
Chocolate financiers, to use up the egg whites.
Preheat the oven to 200 °C and brown the butter.|Cooking|5
Mix the ground almonds, icing sugar, flour, cocoa and egg whites.
Add the brown butter, then the chocolate chips.
Fill the buttered moulds and bake for 12 min.|Oven|12
Little pure butter shortbread biscuits, cut out with a cutter.
Mix the soft butter, sugar, vanilla sugar and a pinch of salt.
Add the egg, then the flour, and shape into a ball without overworking it.
Preheat the oven to 180 °C. Roll out the dough and cut out the biscuits.
Bake for 10 min. They should stay pale.|Oven|10
With the zest of a lemon in the dough.
Mix the soft butter, sugar and lemon zest.
Add the egg, then the flour, and shape into a ball.
Preheat the oven to 180 °C, roll out the dough and cut out the biscuits.
Cocoa shortbread with chips, for chocolate lovers.
Mix the soft butter and sugar, then the egg.
Add the flour, cocoa and chocolate chips, and shape into a ball.
Preheat the oven to 180 °C, roll out the dough and cut out the biscuits.
A soft, stringy brioche for weekend breakfast.
Dissolve the yeast in the lukewarm milk.
Mix the flour, sugar, 1 tsp of salt, 3 eggs and the milk, then knead for 10 min.|Kneading|10
Add the soft butter in pieces and keep kneading until the dough is smooth.
Leave to rise for 1 h 30 under a tea towel.|Rise|90
Shape 6 balls into a loaf tin and leave to rise for another 45 min.|Rise|45
Preheat the oven to 180 °C, brush with the last beaten egg and bake for 30 min.|Oven|30
With chocolate chips in the dough.
The soft tea-time brioche, full of chocolate chips.
Dissolve the yeast in the lukewarm milk, then knead with the flour, sugar, salt and 3 eggs.|Kneading|10
Add the soft butter, then the chocolate chips, while kneading.
Shape into a loaf tin and leave to rise for 45 min.|Rise|45
Brush with the last egg and bake for 30 min at 180 °C.|Oven|30
Shaped into a braid and sprinkled with pearl sugar.
A beautiful braided brioche for the middle of the table.
Dissolve the yeast in the lukewarm milk, then knead with the flour, sugar, salt and 3 eggs.|Kneading|10
Add the soft butter and knead until the dough is smooth.
Divide the dough into 3 ropes and braid them on a baking tray. Leave to rise for 45 min.|Rise|45
Brush with beaten egg, sprinkle with pearl sugar and bake for 25 min at 180 °C.|Oven|25
Soft doughnuts, deep-fried until golden and rolled in sugar.
Dissolve the yeast in the lukewarm milk.
Mix the flour, 50 g of sugar, a pinch of salt, the eggs, the milk and the melted butter, and knead for 5 min.
Roll out the dough to 1 cm, cut out rounds and leave to rise for 30 min.|Rise|30
Fry the doughnuts for 2 min on each side in the hot oil.|Frying|4
Drain them and roll them in the rest of the sugar.
Carnival apple fritters, crisp and soft.
Mix the flour, sugar, eggs and milk into a smooth batter.
Peel the apples, remove the core and cut into rings.
Dip the rings in the batter.
Fry them for 2 min on each side in the hot oil.|Frying|4
Drain and dust with icing sugar.
Pieces of banana in a light batter.
Golden banana fritters, as in the Caribbean.
Mash 2 bananas and mix them with the flour, sugar, cinnamon, egg and milk.
Cut the other bananas into slices and add them to the batter.
Fry spoonfuls of batter for 2 min on each side.|Frying|4
Drain on kitchen paper and serve warm.
